CS5-01.note: The colon appositively glosses the blank ('a residue of manufacture with no bearing on how the sheet aged') = incidental. 'protective' is the revised view, not the discarded one; 'corrosive' is the opposite of the finding; 'deliberate' is unaddressed. Mechanical once the colon is read, hence easy.

CS5-02.note: 'the same terminal trill' forty years apart and the closing 'Stability at forty-year intervals' both point to invariant. 'polymorphic'/'stochastic' are the drift the larger archive finds, i.e. the corrected view, not the assumed one; 'attenuated' has no referent. Vocabulary raises this above easy; the logic itself is one step.

CS5-03.note: Closest call of the four completions. 'imitative' (D) and 'perishable' (B) are each restated verbatim in the very clauses that SUPPORT the blank ('flakes badly', 'copied wholesale from Italian maiolica'), so choosing either makes the sentence circular; the reversal is informational ('little seemed to be lost', 'painful to think about', isotopes assign a kiln) = uninformative. Requires the redundancy test rather than a synonym match, which is genuine module-2 work.

CS5-04.note: 'one hand working once and at leisure' fixes the assumption as a single later sitting = retrospective. (B) contemporaneous is the trap and is directly contradicted by that same clause, yet reads as the natural 'victualling book kept day by day' answer; the UV evidence (eleven ink changes at port calls, later days squeezed into margins the earlier days left) refutes the single sitting. The final sentence fencing off accuracy also kills (A) fabricated cleanly. Best-built item in the batch.

CS5-05.note: 'neither is the quicker to work with' is an explicit blocker for (B) Efficiency, and 'the account that adds fewer unattested entities has the better claim' is a definition of parsimony. The explicit blocker is what keeps this out of hard. (C) Prosperity is dead weight: eliminable blind by register alone on any academic-argument item, which is what makes the set weak.

CS5-06.note: Grammatical subject is 'The diarist's ACCOUNT', which blocks (C) Perceive outright - and (C) is otherwise the reading the four-month delay invites ('it hadn't registered yet'). (D) Indicate fails because the account does indicate the losses factually (bridge, sheep); what is absent is any recognition of them AS loss. (A) Chronicle fails because she chronicles throughout. The item survives on the account/diarist distinction alone - the single most fragile key in the batch, though I believe it holds.

CS5-07.note: Author's own flag is correct and understated. 'Concluded' is the everyday sense of 'settled' and also the key, so the default guess wins; I could have picked it from the stem word alone. The passage only confirms ('satisfied nobody' blocks Quieted, 'nothing in the mechanics justified' blocks Clarified) - it never has to overturn anything, which is the shape every other VIC item in this batch does have.

CS5-08.note: 'It is not spare' is an explicit blocker for the default sense (A) Unadorned, and the whole second half is about a farmer being able to act on it plus 'a report nobody outside the field can read is not a report' = Accessible. (B) Forthright has no candor content anywhere. Blocking the stock sense with one clause is the right move; it caps the item at medium because the blocker is unmissable.

CS5-09.note: Flat boulders hold snow six weeks longer -> less growing season -> boulders' thalli smaller than their age implies (which is why the 1710 date is too young). Full 2x2 over {boulders, gravestones} x {larger, smaller}, so a solver who gets the direction right and the subject wrong lands on a distractor. Two axes and a suppressed-growth inference: honestly hard.

CS5-10.note: The two things the rest of the text actually offers are the fee and the unissued masters - exactly (D). (B) is the near miss: 'a week's wage' really is in the text, but 'the royalty the contracts denied' belongs to sentence 1's setup, not to the evidence tested against it, so (B) mislabels one of its pair. (A) rival label and (C) records sold are absent. Good frame: one sentence, only the trailing pair varies.

CS5-11.note: 'they remain small; the closed stands ... have gone on shrinking behind them' = (C). (D) is a real trap but invents a detection threshold for aerial canopy that the text never states; (B) invents an area equivalence; (A) invents a scale argument. Rejecting (D) requires noticing that 'remain small' is about growth, not about measurability.

CS5-12.note: Two clauses, two reasons: the terms predate the lists (guild rolls carry them throughout) and the form changed in 1806. Both undercut the inferred change in organization. (C) is the pull - the sentence does favour the rolls evidentially - but 'prefer the rolls as evidence about trade' is not what the sentence is for, and it ignores the 1806 clause entirely.

CS5-13.note: The last sentence adds biomass to clear against a per-cut funding model = added workload/cost. (A) is contradicted in direction, (B) describes sentence 1, (D) describes something the text never does. One-step; easy.

CS5-14.note: 'which suggests storage rather than flight' signposts the key inside the passage, so the item is easy whatever the option set does. Author flagged one rejectable option: I make it (A) - explaining the WESTERN pattern by raiding recorded in the EAST is incoherent on its face - rather than (C). Strictly (A) is not eliminable blind, so I keep the set at plausible, but the signposting is the bigger problem here, not the option.

CS5-15.note: 'only by a fifth of the gap' and 'The remainder tracks the concentration of a small solute' are quoted almost intact by (C). Arithmetic matching, no inference. (D)'s 'temperature covering the rest' is near-incoherent since temperature is the condition, not a competing cause.

CS5-16.note: Worse than the author describes. (A) breaks parallelism with the other three: B/C/D all read 'help readers ...', (A) reads 'cost the psalm ...'. That is a blind-eliminable shape tell, not merely a rejectable option - it is exactly the option-family asymmetry CLAUDE.md records as a recurring structural tell. Between the survivors the text names agreement about the turn explicitly, so it is easy with the passage and a 1-in-3 without it.

CS5-17.note: The point of the text is the up-to-six-degree gap found on foot; the overnight park agreement in (A) is the control that rules out sensor error, not the comparison the text is for. (A) is a genuine trap because it is drawn from the passage rather than invented, which lifts this above easy; (B) and (C) are invented.

CS5-18.note: 'the lyre, and no other instrument, accompanies the walk to the church' states the key almost verbatim. (D) is the good distractor and is specifically contradicted - the fiddlers DID travel and came home for the wedding months - but the key is handed over too directly for more than easy.

CS5-19.note: Inversion holds, but only just. (A) actigraphy-scores-stillness-as-sleep is the real-world stock critique and Text 2 NAMES actigraphy in its first sentence while offering not one word of evidence against it; all of Text 2's actual evidence is the door/corridor chain (dose-response on prior corridor brightness, null on the ward whose doors were already done). A solver who reasons from the evidence gets B; a solver who reasons from sleep-science priors is pulled hard at A. The bare mention is bait with a purpose, so I do not call it broken - but it is the one item where the deliberate inversion is closest to failing.

CS5-20.note: Inversion works: (A) legume nitrogen is the field's stock answer and is explicitly neutralized ('every plot is fertilized to the same soil-nitrogen target'), (C) weeds explicitly equalized. But Text 2 then states the alternative cause outright - 'later drilling has raised cereal yield on its own' - so once the two refutations are read the key is handed over. Agree with the author that (D) is rejectable: it is a vague methodological complaint with no anchor in either text, and it is the only option not tied to a stated fact.

CS5-21.note: Text 2 is entirely about the counting change (once-per-visitor vs every entry, shared courtyard) plus a null household survey. (B), (C), (D) are all facts Text 2 never asserts. Clean but one-step.

CS5-22.note: Agreement item: the fall in submissions is the one claim both texts assert (Text 2 disputes the CAUSE, not the fact). (C) is Text 2 only; (B) and (D) are in neither. Agreement items are structurally easy and this one is no exception.

CS5-23.note: 'their recall matches the writers'; their reproduction of the shapes does not' - matched time erases the RECALL gap (so time, not motor rehearsal, explains it) and leaves the REPRODUCTION gap (motor rehearsal). (C) is the exact inversion and is one misread of a compact semicolon clause away; (A) and (D) complete the grid. The one paired item whose key cannot be reached by the 'name the confound Text 2 gives evidence for' shortcut.

CS5-24.note: Inversion holds well: (A) water table is the stock trophic-cascade counter-argument and is explicitly killed ('The water table did not move'), (B) ponds killed ('reaches with ponds gained no more height'), (D) fencing never mentioned. The key requires chaining June/late-August against 'shoots put on most of their length during July', with the same-month reaches as the clincher - two steps, hence medium rather than easy.

CS5-05.detail: The senses do not in fact cluster too tightly: 'neither is the quicker to work with' disjoins Efficiency from Parsimony explicitly, and Arrangement has no support anywhere. The live defect is the opposite one - Prosperity is blind-eliminable dead weight, so the item is really a 3-option question. That costs difficulty, not correctness.

CS5-07.detail: Understated. It is not only that a blind guesser defaults to the everyday sense - the everyday sense is also the key, and the passage never has to overturn anything, it only confirms. Every other VIC item in the batch (05, 06, 08) blocks its stock sense with an explicit clause; 07 blocks two rivals and leaves the default standing. This is the only item in the batch I mark passage_needed false, and it is the weakest item here.

CS5-14.detail: I make the rejectable option (A) (western pattern explained by eastern raiding - incoherent), not (C). But the option set is not the item's problem: 'which suggests storage rather than flight' signposts the key inside the passage, so it grades easy regardless of which option is dropped.

CS5-16.detail: The worst of the four. (A) is not merely rejectable on the passage - it breaks the option-set's parallelism (B/C/D 'help readers ...' vs A 'cost the psalm ...'), so it is eliminable with the source covered. That is a structural tell, and it reduces a supposed module-2 item to 1-in-3 blind. Fix by rewriting (A) as a benefit claim that the text does not support.

CS5-20.detail: (D) is indeed rejectable - the only option with no anchor in either text. Described accurately. Note separately that the item is easy for a reason unrelated to (D): Text 2 states the competing cause in so many words.

template_groups.detail: CS5-19/20/21/24 share one solvable shortcut: Text 2 lists two or three facts, explicitly neutralizes the stock explanations, and the key restates the one confound Text 2 actually supplies evidence for. A solver who learns 'pick the confound Text 2 gives evidence for, never the one it only mentions' clears all four without weighing the options. CS5-23 uses the same paired frame but is not solvable that way (it needs a which-gap-survives-matching mapping), so the tight group is four and the loose group five. Recommend re-shaping at least one of 19/20/21/24 - e.g. make Text 2's evidence support a confound only partially, so the key has to be the qualified one.

6 of 24 (25%) are paired-text items. On the real Digital SAT paired texts are roughly 2 of 54 R&W questions. This is a blueprint-weighting observation, not a defect in any item - flagged only so the batch is not read as representative of the module.

template_groups.template: One-frame options varying a single trailing clause
template_groups.detail: All seven function/structure items hold four options in one syntactic frame and vary only the trailing clause. This is the CLEAN pattern per CLAUDE.md - every option satisfies the stem equally, so only the source discriminates - and it should be kept. Listed here for completeness because it is a shared template, not because it is a tell. The exception is CS5-16, where the frame is broken by one option (see unfixed_items_verdict).
